title: POC scoping: LoadBridge script onboarding & benchmark acceptance
summary: Kickoff scoping for a 4-week POC to validate load and latency SLOs using customer scripts (LoadBridge harness). Discussed success criteria (p95 latency, quality regression tolerance), workload sizing, streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs, telemetry, security needs (VPC, KMS, SOC2 evidence), and timeline/next steps.
topics: Customer scripts: mapping inputs, streaming compatibility
Success criteria: p95 latency, quality/regression thresholds, throughput
Telemetry and artifacts: traces, token-level cost, benchmarks sheet
next_steps: Alex Morgan - share POC playbook + LoadBridge adapter spec - 2027-09-16
Maya Chen - provide canonical customer script set (3 scenarios) and sample dataset - 2027-09-18
Jamal Rivera - schedule 1st integration session and credentials exchange (VPC peering / staging) - 2027-09-20
action_items: Alex Morgan - Export security checklist and SOC2 evidence links to ClearLens - 2027-09-16
Maya Chen - Export anonymized sample trace for cold-start pattern - 2027-09-18
Luis Ortega - Confirm SSO provider (Okta) and share IdP metadata - 2027-09-17
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-14 16:00 UTC
Duration: 63 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Jamal Rivera (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Lead ML Eng, ClearLens), Jordan Patel (CTO), Luis Ortega (SRE)

[00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): hey everyone good afternoon, uh thanks for joining. quick goal for today is to scope the POC around your LoadBridge scripts, map success criteria and timelines. jamal and i will take notes, and we'll capture integration blockers.
[00:18] Maya (ClearLens): thanks alex. im most interested in validating latency at scale and making sure our streaming paths don't regress quality. we use a mix of streaming for interactive UI and non-streaming for batch scoring.
[00:29] Jamal (Redwood SE): great, and do you have a prioritized list of scripts? when you say streaming vs non-streaming, are the payloads identical or does streaming send incremental deltas?
[00:42] Maya (ClearLens): good q. three canonical scenarios: 1) interactive chat (streaming tokens, incremental), 2) batch summarization (non-streaming, larger batched payloads), 3) rerank pipeline (shorter sequences but high qps). we'll send you the script set.
[00:57] Jordan (CTO): just to set constraints: p95 latency target for interactive is 200-250ms, throughput target for rerank is 350-400 req/s, and cost target we talked internally is under $60 per 1M tokens across the POC if possible.
[01:17] Alex: noted. we should break down the acceptance criteria - p95, quality regression tolerance (how much You can accept), and error budget. maya, what is your quality regression tolerance?
[01:30] Maya: ideally <2% regression on our BLEU/ROUGE-equivalent evals. anything above 5% and product won't ship. so acceptance window is 0-2% green, 2-5% yellow.
[01:45] Jamal: good, we'll measure against your eval sets. for load harness integration, there are two parts: adapter for LoadBridge to drive Redwood API and a lightweight collector to capture token-level timing. we have an adapter template, it'll need a couple of hooks for streaming chunking and for KV cache reuse.
[02:06] Luis (SRE): on network — we'll need VPC connectivity. ClearLens policy is to peer to vendor staging during POC and keep production air-gapped. also KMS for key control, and we use Okta for SSO.
[02:22] Alex: we support VPC peering for private deployment and have a staging flow for hosted account with restricted egress. KMS integration is via customer-managed key (HSM-backed) for Private runs; for hosted we can do envelope encryption with customer KMS. okta SAML is supported. we'll share the checklist.
[02:45] Jordan: do you have an example of how telemetry looks? we need tracebacks to correlate cold starts and token-level cost.
[02:53] Jamal: yes — we surface token-level latency, per-route cost breakdowns, and a per-request trace id that can be mapped back to your harness. we'll also attach sampling traces and per-model token histogram. we'll export a sample CSV and a Grafana dashboard.
[03:14] Maya: great. about streaming: we observed some vendor switching behavior where streaming had slightly higher latencies but lower compute cost. can you quantify that?
[03:25] Jamal: streaming trades off per-request overhead against end-to-end latency depending on chunk size. for small interactive prompts, streaming reduces user-observed latency, but it complicates batching and KV reuse. we'll run two benchmark passes: streaming enabled and streaming disabled, with identical input sequences.
[03:46] Alex: timeline proposal: week 0 (this week) - credential exchange and script handoff, week 1 - adapter integration and smoke runs, week 2 - scaled benchmark runs + telemetry collection, week 3 - tuning (quantization/ batching tweaks) + regression checks, week 4 - final acceptance and handoff.
[04:07] Jordan: sounds reasonable. what's the effort for adapter on our side?
[04:12] Jamal: low to medium. if your scripts follow the LoadBridge adapter interface, it should be a day or two of engineering to map the payloads. if you have streaming deltas, we might need an extra day for chunking logic. we'll pair program during the integration session.
[04:31] Luis: regarding compliance, we need SOC2 Type II evidence and audit log retention for 90 days. also, can you provide an encrypted SLA for the dedicated run?
[04:41] Alex: we can provide SOC2 evidence and audit logs for Private and Dedicated customers; hosted can provide obfuscated logs and a compliance pack. SLA for Dedicated is standard — we'll export the contract language and add an addendum for retention.
[04:59] Maya: for success criteria, besides latency and quality, we also want no more than 0.5% 5xx errors during a 1 hour steady-state run at target qps.
[05:11] Jamal: we'll include error rates in the acceptance matrix. we'll set up two steady-state windows: 1 hour and a 6-hour soak if you want deeper confidence.
[05:23] Maya: let's start with 1 hour for the POC, 6-hour soak optional if the first pass is flaky.
[05:30] Jordan: what about model variants — will you fall back if a high-memory variant is needed?
[05:37] Alex: yes we can route by policy — fallback to a quantized variant or different model family. we'll document expected perf delta. if we need on-demand capacity we can provision a dedicated instance for the benchmark window.
[05:50] Jamal: technical note: for KV cache reuse experiments, we need to control for warm vs cold starts. the harness should include a warmup phase where the same conversation prefixes are replayed. otherwise cold-start tail latency will skew p95.
[06:09] Maya: noted. we'll add warmup sequences.
[06:13] Luis: network shaping — we need to simulate realistic client networks, including 50-150ms client RTT. does your harness support client-side network emulation?
[06:23] Jamal: LoadBridge has a driver for network delay injection and jitter. we'll configure profiles to match your telemetry.
[06:30] Alex: ok let's talk about artifacts. we'll share: 1) POC playbook (https://redwood.ai/poc-playbook) 2) LoadBridge adapter spec (attached in follow-up) 3) benchmark sheet template (https://redwood-internal/benchmarks/CL-9981) 4) security checklist.
[06:53] Maya: please add a column in the benchmark sheet for our proprietary quality metric (we call it CL-Score).
[06:59] Jamal: will do. we'll also add columns for p50/p95/p99 token latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1M tokens.
[07:12] Jordan: when you run quantization, we need to see A/B results with the same seed and eval set. reproducibility is important.
[07:20] Jamal: agreed — we'll fix random seeds and snapshot model bits. our Optimize team will recommend quant/kerning settings but we'll keep raw artifacts.
[07:29] Maya: any gotchas around streaming that we should be aware of?
[07:33] Jamal: yes: chunk size and aggregation window are the main levers. small chunks = lower user latency but worse batching efficiency. also, some older models don't support efficient streaming kernels which can blow up GPU utilization. we'll include model compatibility matrix.
[07:52] Luis: on data residency — some of our customers require EU-only residency. for POC it's ok but if we see progress we'll need EU-region tests.
[07:59] Alex: we can run region-targeted benchmarks for the EU region if required; that'll add a parallel run and extra cost.
[08:06] Maya: downtime tolerances — we need a rollback plan during integration in case the harness causes issues in staging.
[08:13] Jamal: we'll run in a dedicated staging project and only use read-only test keys; nothing will touch prod. rollback is simply switching the routing rule back to your existing endpoint.
[08:24] Jordan: how do we validate functional parity? we want to make sure outputs are semantically equivalent within your CL-Score; deterministic checks may fail because of sampling.
[08:36] Jamal: we'll run exact-match and semantic-similarity (embedding cosine) checks; for sampling we'll do n=50 seeds and compare distributions, not single-shot equality.
[08:49] Maya: fico. what about cost accounting? we need per-route attribution and per-token cost captured in the harness.
[08:57] Alex: LoadBridge adapter will emit token counts per request and Redwood will attach per-token cost; the benchmark CSV will include cost columns.
[09:06] Maya: ok. what are the acceptance thresholds again? can you summarize?
[09:09] Alex: sure. acceptance matrix: 1) p95 latency interactive <= 250ms, 2) rerank throughput >= 350 req/s with <0.5% 5xx errors in 1 hour steady-state, 3) quality regression <= 2% on CL-Score, 4) cost <= $60 per 1M tokens, 5) security checklist items satisfied (VPC or dedicated controls, KMS).
[09:36] Luis: is the cost target a hard cap or guidance?
[09:38] Jordan: guidance for POC, but if cost is too high we'll look at dedicated/quantization options.
[09:45] Jamal: we'll run a cost sensitivity sweep — base, quantized 4-bit and mixed precision. we'll report delta to your baseline.
[09:55] Maya: contains a question — will you run both streaming and non-streaming and then we choose the better path?
[09:59] Alex: yes. two full passes identical inputs. provide the scripts; we'll param the harness to toggle streaming.
[10:07] Jamal: integration checklist items: adapter repo fork, idp metadata, VPC peering request, sample scripts location, target bucket for traces. we'll need a staging account owner.
[10:22] Maya: luis will be staging owner. i'll upload scripts to the repo by friday.
[10:28] Luis: ok will do.
[10:30] Alex: any risks you want us to call out?
[10:32] Jordan: main risk is that our rerank throughput requires a different model family with higher VRAM, in which case standard hosted endpoints may not achieve the throughput target.
[10:44] Jamal: contingency: we'll test a compatible model family and if that fails, spin up a Dedicated capacity for the 1-2 benchmark windows. that will add procurement steps but it's doable within the POC timeline if approved.
[11:00] Maya: procurement involvement — we may need an MSA or short-term addendum for dedicated nodes.
[11:06] Alex: noted, i'll loop in our sales ops and legal once we get sign-off.
[11:11] Jamal: technical nit: for reproducing cold starts we recommend synthetic replay at 20% higher qps during warmup to fully fill KV caches. that'll give realistic cache warmness.
[11:26] Maya: okay we'll add that to scripts.
[11:30] Alex: sounds like we're aligned on scope. recap of immediate deliverables — alex shares playbook + adapter spec; maya provides scripts and sample traces; jamal schedules the integration session and prepares a benchmark sheet.
[11:44] Jordan: timeline check: can we aim to start week of 9/20?
[11:48] Alex: yes week of 9/20 for integration. full acceptance target by week of 10/18 (4 weeks).
[11:55] Luis: i'll send the IdP metadata tomorrow.
[11:59] Maya: any other blockers?
[12:02] Jamal: none from our side. we'll also include a short post-run checklist to validate reproducibility and artifact completeness.
[12:11] Alex: ok let's close with concrete next steps and owners.
[12:15] Maya: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[12:17] Alex: thanks all, we'll follow up with the playbook and sheet. talk soon.

Notes and references: POC playbook link (sent follow-up), LoadBridge adapter template attached in follow-up email, benchmark sheet template: https://redwood-internal/benchmarks/CL-9981, security checklist: will attach SOC2 extracts and KMS integration notes.

End of transcript.
